title: Distill lessons from failures as well as successes
rule: For web and coding agents with persistent experience memory, retrieve concise strategies distilled from both successful and failed attempts rather than keeping only successful routines.
boundary: Outcomes must be judgeable; the evidence does not establish transfer to tasks with ambiguous success.

title: Keep evaluation tasks out of the improvement loop
rule: When evolving a harness, use disjoint tasks for improvement and final evaluation; do not interpret a promotion set repeatedly consulted during selection as an untouched test.
boundary: Disjoint evaluation limits one source of leakage; it does not establish generalization across every task or backbone.

title: Promote a patch only after checking what it could break
rule: For recurring agent workflows, test candidate skills on their targeted failures, protected regression cases, and negative controls before promotion.
boundary: The most direct gated-versus-ungated evidence is from SEC-filing QA; independent cross-domain reproduction is still needed.

title: Evolve harness modules separately before integrating
rule: For modular coding and terminal-agent harnesses, compare independent module improvements with a joint rewrite before adopting a new harness.
boundary: One evolving backbone supplies the main ablation; interactions between independently improved modules still need integration checks.

title: Diagnose recurring failures before turning them into rules
rule: When aggregating failure traces across tasks, add a separate attribution stage before writing harness edits so repeated symptoms do not simply become model-specific accommodations.
boundary: One paper provides the comparison; its failure-attribution labels and taxonomy need independent checking.

title: Ground self-correction in evidence beyond the answer
rule: For reasoning tasks, require an external signal such as a test or verifier before treating self-critique as a reliable improvement.
boundary: This concerns review-and-revise reasoning, not a claim that every model judgment is useless; aggregate experience-memory labeling may tolerate noise.

title: Run available mechanical checks before model judgment
rule: In a verify-and-fix loop, use relevant executable checks for properties they actually test, then calibrate any model judge used for the remaining properties.
boundary: The ordering is partly mechanism-based guidance, not a universal measured ranking. Rule-dense long-context tasks may gain more from a clear checklist than extra verifier execution.

title: Keep iterative UI repairs narrow
rule: For screenshot-guided UI-to-code refinement, choose one scoped repair target per round and carry earlier targets forward as constraints.
boundary: Evidence is from UI reconstruction benchmarks with substantial model-based judging; arbitrary product redesign is outside the tested setup.

title: Represent unusable tool results as failures
rule: When a tool cannot return a usable value, make the response envelope report an error rather than status:ok with missing or redacted data.
boundary: The experiment used stub tools and limited human label validation. Production failure distributions and access-denied semantics need testing.

title: Retrieve more history only while it helps
rule: For retrieval-augmented personalization, compare adaptive stopping with a fixed retrieval budget rather than assuming more user history improves answers.
boundary: The measured optimum depends on six LaMP tasks and frozen 8-9B generators; the reported best k is not a general default.

title: Treat retrieval as an evidence channel with its own failure modes
rule: When grounding answers in retrieved content, inspect source trust and conflicting accounts rather than assuming retrieval makes the answer reliable.
boundary: Separate instructions from source data and evaluate the actual retrieval channel; ordinary relevant documents and adversarial content have different failure profiles.

title: Measure whether a repository guide improves the work
rule: Before growing a coding-agent context file, compare task outcomes and cost against a no-file baseline.
boundary: The benchmark comparison is Python-only and not a test of every failure-specific practitioner guide. Do not generalize it into a ban on repository instructions.

title: Measure task quality alongside token savings
rule: When adopting an efficiency-oriented harness optimization, compare each component and the full stack on both task quality and resource use.
boundary: The cited stack is a single-run study without variance; a small score decrease may be an acceptable deliberate trade, not a failure.

title: Do not broadcast every agent context by default
rule: In multi-agent tasks where one wrong fact can cascade, compare selective information sharing against full-context broadcast.
boundary: The seeded-error effect was task-dependent, absent in the software setting, and measured with one model and small samples.

title: Test coordination ideas against a matched architecture
rule: For multi-agent literature synthesis, compare a learned coordinator with a simpler coordinator given the same workspace and action space.
boundary: The reported learned-versus-LLM coordination difference is within potential judge noise; no general conclusion about all learned coordination follows.

title: Compare agent pruning with a budget-matched random control
rule: When optimizing a multi-agent topology, hold the backbone, roles, runtime and structural budget fixed and compare with random pruning.
boundary: The finding concerns the tested methods and topologies; it is not proof that optimized pruning can never help.

title: Check reasoning steps to localize the repair
rule: For chain-of-thought verification, compare per-node consistency checks with whole-chain judging when locating an error is the goal.
boundary: The gains concern public reasoning benchmarks, not arbitrary agent traces; the proposed attention mechanism was not directly isolated.

title: Obtain an answer before supplying the preferred conclusion
rule: When a task does not require the user’s opinion, withhold it until after the initial answer to reduce one trigger for sycophantic agreement.
boundary: Personalization sometimes requires preferences. This is not a reason to omit relevant user requirements or a guarantee against every form of sycophancy.
